stories.title: 📜 Psalms of Solomon
summaryBullets: A collection of eighteen Jewish psalms from the late 1st century BCE, composed in response to Jerusalem’s conquest by Pompey in 63 BCE and not included in later biblical canons.

They blend nationalistic lament, calls for righteousness, and Messianic hope—portraying the Messiah as a righteous, David-like deliverer who will rescue Israel, including the earliest use of the title “Son of David.”
The tone shifts between corporate confession, denunciation of Israel’s leaders, and trust in God’s justice, often urging personal and communal repentance.
Though originally written in Hebrew or Aramaic, the collection survives only in Greek and Syriac manuscripts; they were grouped under Solomon’s name—likely for prestige, not authorship.
crossRefs: 2 Samuel 7:12–16 — God’s covenant promises to David’s house.
Isaiah 11:1–2 — Messianic expectation of a righteous shoot from Jesse.
Matthew 21:9 — 'Son of David' as title applied to Jesus in the Gospels.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֶּן־דָּוִד (ben-Dāwīḏ) — Greek: υἱὸς Δαυὶδ (huios Dauid) — Aramaic: בּר דָּוִד (bar Dāwīḏ)
translationNotes.note: An early explicit title for the Messiah here, emphasizing dynastic and hopeful expectations of a righteous king from David’s line.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Psalms of Solomon give voice to first-century BCE Jewish hopes amid oppression, urging moral reform and Messianic deliverance.
